title: Hymyilevä neito tiskin takana
subtitle: Appendix 5 — the last miscellany, closing out full corpus coverage

blocks.text: This is the true leftover pile — vivid one-off details that never fit neatly into a grammar lesson: a lawnmower repair, a winter breakdown on the highway, a smiling face behind the counter. After this, there's no vocabulary left in the corpus you haven't met.

blocks.content: {Neito|word|noun|young woman/maiden} is a slightly old-fashioned, warm word for a young woman — hymyilevä neito tiskin takana, 'a smiling young woman behind the counter'. {Tiski|word|noun|counter} is the service counter itself. {Piristävä|word|adjective|uplifting/refreshing} describes something that brightens your mood. {Kohdella|word|verb|to treat (someone)} is how a customer describes being handled: minua kohdeltiin ystävällisesti.

items.fi: Hymyilevä {neito|word|noun|young woman} oli {piristävä|word|adjective|uplifting} lisä {tiskin|grammar|genitive of tiski|the counter's} takana.
items.en: A smiling young woman was an uplifting addition behind the counter.

items.fi: Minua {kohdeltiin|grammar|passive past of kohdella|was treated} ystävällisesti.

blocks.text: The lawnmower and the winter breakdown

blocks.content: Two vivid stories in the corpus bring their own small vocabulary clusters. The lawnmower repair: {ruohonleikkuri|word|compound noun|lawnmower} (ruoho, grass + leikkuri, cutter), {koppa|word|noun|hopper/bin}, and {hitsaustyö|word|compound noun|welding work}. The winter highway breakdown: {ahtoletku|word|compound noun|turbo hose}, {pakkanen|word|noun|frost/freezing cold}, {rekka|word|noun|truck/lorry}, {jyrätä|word|verb|to thunder/roll past}, and {kyynärvarsi|word|compound noun|forearm}.

items.fi: {Ruohonleikkurin|grammar|genitive of ruohonleikkuri|the lawnmower's} {kopan|grammar|genitive of koppa|hopper's} pieni {hitsaustyö|word|compound noun|welding work} tehtiin joustavasti.
items.en: The lawnmower hopper's small welding job was done flexibly.

items.fi: {Ahtoletku|word|compound noun|turbo hose} oli jätetty löysälle kymmenen asteen {pakkasessa|grammar|inessive of pakkanen|in the frost}.
items.en: The turbo hose had been left loose in ten degrees of frost.

items.fi: {Rekkojen|grammar|genitive plural of rekka|trucks'} {jyrätessä|grammar|second infinitive of jyrätä|as [they] thundered past} vierestä, jouduin korjaamaan kädet {kyynärvarsiin|grammar|illative plural of kyynärvarsi|up to the forearms} asti öljyssä.
items.en: As trucks thundered past, I had to repair it with my hands up to the forearms in oil.

blocks.content: {Ahdas|word|adjective|cramped/tight} describes a too-small parking lot — ahdas piha, mentioned in more than one review as a minor complaint. {Lommo|word|noun|dent} appears in the corpus's harshest review, describing damage caused during a repair. {Maine|word|noun|reputation}, {neuvotella|word|verb|to negotiate}, and {joustoa|grammar|partitive of jousto|flexibility} round out the workplace-interaction vocabulary.

items.en: The cramped yard made parking difficult.

items.fi: Autoon tehty {lommoja|grammar|partitive plural of lommo|dents} asentajan työkaluilla.
items.en: Dents made to the car with the mechanic's tools.

items.fi: Hyvä {maine|word|noun|reputation}, ja oli valmis {neuvottelemaan|grammar|third infinitive, illative|to negotiate} hinnasta.
items.en: Good reputation, and was willing to negotiate on price.

blocks.content: {Vikakoodi|word|compound noun|fault code} (vika + koodi) is the diagnostic code a mechanic reads from a car's computer. {Lukulaite|word|compound noun|reading device/scanner} (lukea, to read + laite, device) is the scanner itself. {Tiedonsiirtohäiriö|word|compound noun|data-transfer disruption} — tieto (data) + siirto (transfer) + häiriö (disruption) — was the excuse one shop gave for a slow diagnosis, referenced back in the colloquial appendix.

items.fi: Kesti tunnin lukea {vikakoodit|word|compound noun, plural|fault codes}.
items.en: It took an hour to read the fault codes.

lines.speaker: A
lines.en: What feeling did the visit leave you with?

lines.speaker: B
lines.fi: Hyvä. Hymyilevä neito tiskin takana oli piristävä lisä, ja minua kohdeltiin ystävällisesti.
lines.en: Good. A smiling young woman behind the counter was an uplifting addition, and I was treated kindly.

lines.speaker: B
lines.en: A bit cramped, but it didn't matter.

blocks.title: Paul Noble Rule
blocks.text: This appendix closes the loop: everything that was ever a genuine one-off in the corpus now has a home. From here, any new Finnish text you read will inevitably contain words outside even this expanded vocabulary — and that's fine. The forty core lessons gave you the grammar engine to decode new words forever; these five appendix lessons just mopped up what that engine alone couldn't guess from context.

blocks.content: Neito: NEI-to (the 'ei' glides like English 'ay'). Ruohonleikkuri: RUO-hon-leik-ku-ri (long compound, break at ruoho-leikkuri). Kyynärvarsi: KYY-när-var-si (long held 'yy', the 'ä' like 'a' in 'cat').
